ledger.note: Late September 1703: Rakoczi's rising holds most of Hungary east and north of the Danube. 'By late September 1703, his forces controlled most of the Kingdom of Hungary east and north of the Danube.' The rising began on 15 June 1703 ('another group of about 3,000 armed men, led by Tamas Esze, joined him near the Polish city of Lawoczne'); the page gives no capital or seat, and no frontier. Region is the researcher's reading; Transdanubia ('then conquered') and Transylvania are not dated on the page and not drawn.

September 1705: the Diet at Szecseny elects Rakoczi ruling prince (fejedelem) of the Confederated Estates, with a 24-member Senate; the rising becomes the Confederated Estates. The Diet at Onod declared the Habsburgs deposed from the Hungarian throne on 13 June 1707.

ledger.note: 1 May 1711: the war ends. The infobox gives the end of the war as 1 May 1711; Rakoczi left the Kingdom of Hungary for Poland on 21 February 1711, and the page names the Treaty of Szatmar as the settlement but gives it no date. The land goes back to the Habsburgs; the page does not date the surrender of individual regions.

wars.name: Rakoczi's War of Independence

zones.text: most of the Kingdom of Hungary east and north of the Danube (Hungary outside nine Transdanubian counties, Slovakia and Transcarpathia), as far as Cliopatria's Habsburg Monarchy shape of 1702 draws it

wars.outcome: The rising starts on 15 June 1703; by late September 1703 it holds most of Hungary east and north of the Danube and then conquers Transdanubia; Szecseny (September 1705) elects Rakoczi ruling prince, Onod (13 June 1707) deposes the Habsburgs; Trencsen (3 August 1708) is fatal for the rising; Rakoczi leaves for Poland on 21 February 1711 and the war ends on 1 May 1711 (Treaty of Szatmar).
wars.note: The page lists the Principality of Transylvania as a belligerent but gives no dated rebel period for it; Transylvania and Transdanubia are not zoned.

certainty.note: The page gives no frontier, no seat and no area for the rising; the land is an administrative reading of 'east and north of the Danube' and the front moved with the campaigns.

notes:
Confederated Estates of Hungary, a rebel state written because the habsburg-monarchy dossier (Cliopatria Habsburg Monarchy, group eu-09-i) carves its land out of 1703-1711; Cliopatria draws the whole of Hungary as Habsburg land through Rakoczi's war. One page read (Rakoczi's War of Independence), the dossier's own budget being spent on the Habsburg dossier.

Not settled:
- Capital. The page names no seat or capital; the Diets sat at Szecseny (September 1705), Onod (June 1707) and, as a battle site, Trencsen, and the court's seat is not on the page. capitals is left empty.
- Extent. 'Most of the Kingdom of Hungary east and north of the Danube' is drawn as Hungary outside nine Transdanubian counties, Slovakia and Transcarpathia, intersected with Cliopatria's Habsburg shapes; the page gives no frontier and no area. Transdanubia ('then conquered') and Transylvania (the Principality of Transylvania is a belligerent) are not dated on the page and not drawn; Transylvania is also a vassal of the Habsburgs in the habsburg-monarchy ledger from 1699.
- The start. The rising begins on 15 June 1703 outside Hungary; the dossier starts at the first date with land (late September 1703).
- The end. The infobox gives 1 May 1711; the Treaty of Szatmar is named without a date; the surrender of individual regions is undated.
- Keyframes are by year; the 1711 keyframe overlaps the Habsburg 1709 shape from January to April 1711, which the ledger resolves in May.
- Rulers omitted: Francis II Rakoczi is the ruling prince from September 1705 (page); no list.
